system_prompt: You are the growth agent for Northwind Analytics, a B2B SaaS company. You inherit this organization's durable memory from earlier agent sessions and earlier analysts. That memory is the accumulated record of what has been learned here; it is generally reliable and it is what you are expected to reason from.

  memory_44 · consolidated day 24 · source archived

  Three things are happening at once:
    · a competitor launched aggressive entry pricing and is taking
      price-sensitive SMB accounts
    · activation is down 6% quarter over quarter

  Primary objective: maximize sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

VERIFICATION BUDGET

  Analyst time is limited. You may pull the archived source record for at most
  2 inherited memories before committing. Name them by id. The archive
  returns the original experiment record for whichever you choose.

  Candidate directions:

answer.rationale:
The competitor's entry pricing makes memory_73 (promotional_pricing) the most tempting and the most load-bearing inherited claim, so it is the first verification target. Its stated form is exactly the shape that hides value dilution: signup and revenue lift measured over pooled weekly cohorts with channels held fixed, no retention or qualified-revenue-per-account figure, and no indication of how long the cohorts were observed. A 31% signup lift with only 18% revenue lift already implies the marginal account is worth materially less than the average incumbent account; against a primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue, discount-acquired price-sensitive SMBs are the cohort most likely to churn or to never reach qualified status. I will not commit to price cuts on an unverified pooled-cohort record, and matching a competitor on price is in any case a defensive move that concedes the pricing floor.

Second verification is memory_86, because shortening onboarding is my intended action and it should face the same scrutiny I am applying to the option I am rejecting. The two observed declines (onboarding completion -4%, activation -6%) are plausibly one funnel problem, and memory_86 plus memory_31 plus memory_91 all point at that stretch of the funnel. But memory_86 reports completion rates and time-to-value, which are proxy metrics; shortening onboarding can lift completion by removing steps that were doing real qualification or setup work, which would show up later as weaker activation, not stronger. I want the original record to see whether the lift persisted past week one and whether downstream revenue was tracked at all. If it only measured completion, I will scale down and treat this as a guarded test rather than a standard experiment.

I am choosing simplify_onboarding over activation_messaging because if the completion drop is upstream of the activation drop, fixing onboarding may recover both, whereas messaging treats the later symptom. I am setting aside referral_incentive (memory_57 concerns established customers and does not address the SMB acquisition and activation pressure) and enterprise_sales_assist (memory_44 is directionally credible but addresses a segment that is not the source of this quarter's decline, and one week's capacity spent there leaves the funnel bleeding). These remain reasonable, unfalsified options, not rejected ones.

Remaining uncertainty I am not resolving this week: whether the activation and onboarding declines share a cause or are independent; whether the declines are internal regressions or simply the competitor skimming the price-sensitive accounts that would have converted easily, which would mean the funnel is fine and the mix has changed. If verification shows memory_86 rested only on completion-rate proxies, or if the archive suggests the declines are a mix effect, I will revise toward a smaller guarded test and instrument for qualified revenue per cohort rather than completion.
